2. Update the `package.json` to reflect the new minimum supported Node.js version:
   ```json
   "engines": {
     "node": ">=18"

   ```

We recommend _never_ using `NODE_ENV`. Set it to "production" in all environments and do not rely on it. If your app, for some reason, needs to know about the "kind" of environment it is running under, use your own variable like `APP_ENV` or something (though relying on such a variable is an antipattern in and of itself). The `NODE_ENV` variable not being set to "production" _will_ cause you issues at some point, as there many libraries out there assuming people are using it and enabling all sorts of non-performant paths when it is not set correctly.

comments.author: iifawzi
comments.body:
Hi, I have an interest in working on this, and I've walked through the code to get myself more familiar with how things work.

Here's how I'm thinking of supporting this: 

I would change how this piece of code is behaving to have multiple schemas for the same status code
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/224dc104260ad26f9baa0e46962f917963d41fe5/lib/validation.js#L19-L26

So maybe if we detected that the `schema` is an array (different content types are needed) the final `acc[statusCode]` should be an object that has the content types as a key where each has it's  specific compiled schema as a value
```js
acc[statusCode] = {
  "application/json":  .....
  "image/png": ........
}

```

and then this will necessitate a change in how the `getSchemaSerializer` function is working on getting the schema serializer to be based on the `status code` and the `content type` 
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/16e4b5bb1dbad1772572d9247694259f2419510e/lib/schemas.js#L135

comments.author: metcoder95
comments.body:
Just adding my tiny two cents, I agree 100% with the points about adding JSDoc across the codebase, most important on those points where a variable is set in a previous point and there are several dependencies down-level and across callbacks within the same function or even script.

Along with the previous point, one of the things that I've seen more friction (and I also have struggled to draw a mental map of it), is how the loading of plugins/routes works in mix with `avvio`.
That can also be accompanied by @mcollina point of handling better those plugins that require to be `await`ed to work (e.g. those ones that set an `onRoute` hook), which has been subjected to quite a good number of opened issues due to plugins not working due to not waiting for them to be loaded.
